paths.learner_scope: Aspiring-to-junior Business Analysts who have prerequisite professional communication and basic business literacy assumed from other paths, but who may have zero prior exposure to spreadsheets, SQL, or BI dashboard tooling -- this path teaches those from scratch rather than assuming them. This path covers the full BA practice: requirements elicitation and documentation, stakeholder facilitation, business process modeling in BPMN, conceptual data modeling, SQL for business reporting, BI dashboard authoring in Power BI and Tableau, spreadsheet-based data analysis, gap analysis and solution evaluation, requirements prioritization, agile BA delivery practices, and professional business communication. Excludes Data Analyst/Data Science responsibilities (Python scripting, statistical modeling, machine learning), Product Management ownership, Software Engineering, Project Management authority, domain-specific regulatory compliance, and Enterprise Architecture.

toc_location.tile_title: Scoping the Problem and Direct Elicitation
toc_location.tile_summary: Define the problem boundary before eliciting solutions, then gather requirements directly through one-on-one interviews and facilitated group workshops.

concepts.primary_objective: Define the problem statement and boundary of a BA effort before eliciting solution requirements.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a vague business complaint, can the learner write a bounded problem statement with clear in/out-of-scope lines?
concepts.practice_objective: Convert a vague stakeholder complaint into a one-paragraph problem statement with explicit scope boundaries.
concepts.central_mental_model: A problem statement fixes what's being solved so elicitation doesn't drift into solving the wrong thing.

toc_location.tile_title: Scoping the Problem and Direct Elicitation
toc_location.tile_summary: Define the problem boundary before eliciting solutions, then gather requirements directly through one-on-one interviews and facilitated group workshops.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The International Institute of Business Analysis and its Business Analysis Body of Knowledge, referenced as the source standard for elicitation technique naming, not taught as separate content.

concepts.primary_objective: Plan and run a structured one-on-one stakeholder interview using a fixed question set to elicit requirements.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a stakeholder profile, can the learner draft and conduct an interview that surfaces specific, testable requirements rather than vague wishes?
concepts.practice_objective: Conduct a mock structured interview with a single stakeholder persona and produce a list of elicited requirement statements.
concepts.central_mental_model: An interview is a controlled, repeatable question protocol for extracting one stakeholder's known needs.

toc_location.tile_title: Scoping the Problem and Direct Elicitation
toc_location.tile_summary: Define the problem boundary before eliciting solutions, then gather requirements directly through one-on-one interviews and facilitated group workshops.

concepts.primary_objective: Plan and run a facilitated group workshop (e.g. a JAD session) to elicit requirements from multiple stakeholders at once.
concepts.assessment_target: Can the learner design a workshop agenda and facilitate it to converge a group of stakeholders on a shared requirement set?
concepts.practice_objective: Design an agenda for a 90-minute requirements workshop and run it with a small stakeholder group.
concepts.central_mental_model: A workshop trades interview depth for group consensus speed by eliciting from many stakeholders simultaneously.

toc_location.tile_summary: Gather requirements through surveys, document review, and observation, then validate and verify what has been elicited for completeness and testability.

concepts.primary_objective: Design a survey/questionnaire to elicit requirements or preferences from a large or dispersed stakeholder population.
concepts.assessment_target: Can the learner write unbiased, answerable survey questions and choose when a survey beats an interview?
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a 10-question stakeholder requirements survey and justify each question.
concepts.central_mental_model: A survey scales elicitation across many respondents at the cost of follow-up depth.

toc_location.tile_summary: Gather requirements through surveys, document review, and observation, then validate and verify what has been elicited for completeness and testability.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A shared location (e.g. a wiki or document library) where existing organizational documents are stored, mentioned only as the place documents are pulled from.

concepts.primary_objective: Extract requirements and constraints by systematically reviewing existing artifacts (contracts, manuals, prior specs).
concepts.assessment_target: Given a sample document, can the learner extract explicit and implied requirements from it?
concepts.practice_objective: Review a sample business document and produce a list of requirements it implies.
concepts.central_mental_model: Existing documents encode requirements someone already wrote down; analysis is mining, not inventing.

toc_location.tile_summary: Gather requirements through surveys, document review, and observation, then validate and verify what has been elicited for completeness and testability.

concepts.primary_objective: Elicit requirements by watching users perform their actual work (job shadowing) rather than asking them to describe it.
concepts.assessment_target: Can the learner distinguish what a worker does from what they say they do, based on an observation session?
concepts.practice_objective: Observe (or review a recorded) task walkthrough and log the gap between stated and actual process steps.
concepts.central_mental_model: People are unreliable narrators of their own workflow; watching reveals what asking misses.

toc_location.tile_summary: Gather requirements through surveys, document review, and observation, then validate and verify what has been elicited for completeness and testability.

concepts.primary_objective: Verify that a set of requirements is complete, unambiguous, and testable, and validate that it matches the actual business need.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a requirements list, can the learner distinguish a validation defect (wrong need) from a verification defect (bad requirement wording)?
concepts.practice_objective: Review a flawed requirements list, classify each defect as a validation or verification issue, and fix it.
concepts.central_mental_model: Verification asks 'is it written right?'; validation asks 'is it the right thing?' -- two different quality checks.

concepts.concept_name: Prototyping and Wireframing for Requirements Elicitation

toc_location.tile_summary: Additional techniques for surfacing requirements and risks: low-fidelity prototyping, brainstorming, focus groups, and requirement risk identification.

concepts.primary_objective: Use low-fidelity prototypes/wireframes as an elicitation tool to surface requirements stakeholders can't articulate verbally.
concepts.assessment_target: Can the learner produce a wireframe from partial requirements and use it to extract new/corrected requirements from a stakeholder's reaction?
concepts.practice_objective: Sketch a low-fidelity wireframe for a described screen and list the new requirements a stakeholder's reaction to it would reveal.
concepts.central_mental_model: Showing beats telling: a rough visual makes people react with requirements they couldn't state in the abstract.

toc_location.tile_summary: Additional techniques for surfacing requirements and risks: low-fidelity prototyping, brainstorming, focus groups, and requirement risk identification.

concepts.primary_objective: Facilitate a divergent-thinking brainstorming session to generate a wide candidate set of ideas or requirements before narrowing.
concepts.assessment_target: Can the learner run a brainstorming session that suspends judgment and produces a broad, unfiltered idea set?
concepts.practice_objective: Run a timed brainstorming session on a given problem and capture the raw idea list without filtering.
concepts.central_mental_model: Brainstorming separates idea generation from idea evaluation to avoid premature narrowing.

toc_location.tile_summary: Additional techniques for surfacing requirements and risks: low-fidelity prototyping, brainstorming, focus groups, and requirement risk identification.

concepts.primary_objective: Run a moderated focus group discussion to elicit requirements or reactions from a representative stakeholder sample.
concepts.assessment_target: Can the learner moderate a focus group to surface consensus and disagreement among participants on a topic?
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a moderator guide for a focus group session on a given product change.
concepts.central_mental_model: A focus group elicits the shape of group opinion, not just individual answers, through moderated interaction.

toc_location.tile_summary: Additional techniques for surfacing requirements and risks: low-fidelity prototyping, brainstorming, focus groups, and requirement risk identification.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify risks embedded in a set of requirements that could threaten project or requirement success.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a requirements list, can the learner flag which requirements carry delivery, compliance, or adoption risk?
concepts.practice_objective: Review a requirements list and tag each with a risk level and a one-line rationale.
concepts.central_mental_model: Requirements can hide risk (ambiguity, dependency, infeasibility) that only surfaces if you look for it deliberately.

toc_location.tile_summary: Author a Business Requirements Document and translate it into a detailed Functional Specification.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Common industry abbreviation for Business Requirements Document, used interchangeably with the full term.

concepts.primary_objective: Author a Business Requirements Document (BRD) that captures business need, objectives, and high-level requirements for sign-off.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a set of elicited requirements, can the learner assemble them into a properly structured BRD?
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a BRD section (objectives, scope, requirements list) from a given elicitation summary.
concepts.central_mental_model: A BRD is the formal business-level contract stating what problem is being solved and why, before solution design.

toc_location.tile_summary: Author a Business Requirements Document and translate it into a detailed Functional Specification.

concepts.primary_objective: Author a Functional Specification that translates business requirements into detailed system behavior.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a business requirement, can the learner write a functional spec section describing precise expected system behavior?
concepts.practice_objective: Convert one BRD requirement into a detailed functional specification entry.
concepts.central_mental_model: A functional spec answers 'exactly how should the system behave,' one level more precise than a business requirement.

toc_location.tile_summary: Write user stories with acceptance criteria and use case specifications as alternate detailed-requirement formats.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The plain-text Given-When-Then syntax convention this concept's acceptance criteria are written in, named as the format standard, not taught as a separate tool.

concepts.primary_objective: Write a user story in standard format with Given-When-Then acceptance criteria that make it independently testable.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a feature idea, can the learner write a well-formed user story with acceptance criteria in Gherkin syntax?
concepts.practice_objective: Convert a feature idea into a user story with 2-3 Given-When-Then acceptance criteria.
concepts.central_mental_model: A user story plus acceptance criteria is a requirement written as a testable promise, not just a description.

toc_location.tile_summary: Write user stories with acceptance criteria and use case specifications as alternate detailed-requirement formats.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A use-case-diagramming term for a user or system that interacts with the system under discussion, mentioned in passing when describing use case structure.

concepts.primary_objective: Write a use case specification describing actor goals, main flow, and alternate flows for a system interaction.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an actor and a goal, can the learner write a use case with a main success scenario and at least one alternate flow?
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a use case (actor, precondition, main flow, one alternate flow) for a given system goal.
concepts.central_mental_model: A use case documents interaction as actor-goal-driven flows, capturing branches a simple user story omits.

toc_location.tile_summary: Trace requirements to their source, manage their lifecycle from draft to retirement, and capture non-functional requirements.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Downstream deliverables (design documents, test cases) the traceability matrix links back to -- referenced by name as what gets linked, not taught as separate content in this path.

concepts.primary_objective: Build and maintain a requirements traceability matrix linking requirements to their source, design, and test artifacts.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a requirement and downstream artifacts, can the learner build a traceability link and identify an orphaned requirement?
concepts.practice_objective: Build a small RTM linking 5 requirements to their source and a test case each.
concepts.central_mental_model: Traceability is a bidirectional map so no requirement is lost and no delivered feature lacks a justified origin.

toc_location.tile_summary: Trace requirements to their source, manage their lifecycle from draft to retirement, and capture non-functional requirements.

concepts.primary_objective: Manage a requirement's lifecycle from draft through approval, change, and retirement, tracking version and status.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a requirement change request, can the learner apply the correct lifecycle state transition and versioning?
concepts.practice_objective: Process a sample change request against a requirement, updating its status and version history.
concepts.central_mental_model: A requirement has a life -- proposed, approved, changed, retired -- and losing track of state causes scope drift.

toc_location.tile_summary: Trace requirements to their source, manage their lifecycle from draft to retirement, and capture non-functional requirements.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify and write non-functional requirements (performance, security, usability, reliability) distinct from functional behavior.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a functional requirement, can the learner identify and write the relevant NFRs it implies?
concepts.practice_objective: Write 3 NFRs (with measurable targets) implied by a given functional requirement.
concepts.central_mental_model: NFRs describe how well the system must behave, not what it must do -- quality attributes, not features.

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify and classify stakeholders, then place them on an influence-interest grid and a RACI matrix to determine engagement approach.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify all stakeholders for an initiative and classify them by role, interest, and authority.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a project brief, can the learner produce a stakeholder list correctly classified by role/type?
concepts.practice_objective: Build a stakeholder register from a given project brief, classifying each entry.
concepts.central_mental_model: Not all stakeholders matter equally; classification is the first filter for who to engage and how.

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify and classify stakeholders, then place them on an influence-interest grid and a RACI matrix to determine engagement approach.

concepts.primary_objective: Place stakeholders on an influence-interest (power-interest) grid to determine engagement strategy per quadrant.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a stakeholder list, can the learner correctly plot each on the influence-interest grid and justify the placement?
concepts.practice_objective: Plot 6 stakeholders on an influence-interest grid and state the engagement approach for each quadrant.
concepts.central_mental_model: Engagement effort should scale with a stakeholder's influence and interest, not be uniform across everyone.

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify and classify stakeholders, then place them on an influence-interest grid and a RACI matrix to determine engagement approach.

concepts.primary_objective: Build a RACI matrix assigning Responsible/Accountable/Consulted/Informed roles across tasks and stakeholders.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a task list and a stakeholder list, can the learner assign correct RACI roles without duplicate Accountable owners?
concepts.practice_objective: Build a RACI matrix for a 5-task mini-project.
concepts.central_mental_model: RACI makes role ambiguity visible by forcing exactly one Accountable owner per task.

toc_location.tile_summary: Plan stakeholder engagement, facilitate meetings and workshops, and apply consensus-building and conflict-resolution techniques.

concepts.primary_objective: Create a stakeholder engagement plan defining communication frequency, channel, and approach per stakeholder group.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a stakeholder register, can the learner produce an engagement plan matching method to stakeholder need?
concepts.practice_objective: Draft an engagement plan row (channel, frequency, owner) for 3 stakeholder groups.
concepts.central_mental_model: Engagement planning turns stakeholder analysis into a concrete, repeatable communication commitment.

toc_location.tile_summary: Plan stakeholder engagement, facilitate meetings and workshops, and apply consensus-building and conflict-resolution techniques.

concepts.primary_objective: Apply facilitation techniques (agenda control, time-boxing, managing dominant voices) to run any effective meeting or workshop.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a meeting scenario with a facilitation problem (e.g. one voice dominating), can the learner apply the correct facilitation technique?
concepts.practice_objective: Given a disruptive meeting scenario, choose and justify a facilitation technique to resolve it.
concepts.central_mental_model: Facilitation is a general skill set for keeping any group meeting productive, independent of the meeting's topic.

toc_location.tile_summary: Plan stakeholder engagement, facilitate meetings and workshops, and apply consensus-building and conflict-resolution techniques.

concepts.primary_objective: Apply consensus-building and conflict-resolution techniques when stakeholders disagree on requirements or priorities.
concepts.assessment_target: Given two stakeholders in conflict, can the learner apply a specific technique to move them toward resolution?
concepts.practice_objective: Role-play resolving a two-stakeholder requirement disagreement using a named conflict-resolution technique.
concepts.central_mental_model: Disagreement between stakeholders needs a deliberate resolution technique, not just more discussion.

toc_location.tile_summary: Learn BPMN 2.0 core notation, then model an existing (as-is) process and a redesigned (to-be) process.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The Object Management Group, the standards body that publishes the BPMN specification; named only as the source of the notation, not taught as content.
A BPMN diagram convention that groups activities by the participant responsible for them, mentioned as a notation element.

concepts.primary_objective: Read and draw BPMN 2.0 core notation elements (events, tasks, gateways, sequence/message flows) correctly.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a process description, can the learner select the correct BPMN symbol for each step?
concepts.practice_objective: Draw a 5-step process using correct BPMN core notation.
concepts.central_mental_model: BPMN is a shared symbol vocabulary so any reader interprets a process diagram the same way.

toc_location.tile_summary: Learn BPMN 2.0 core notation, then model an existing (as-is) process and a redesigned (to-be) process.

concepts.primary_objective: Model an existing (as-is) business process in BPMN to document current-state behavior.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a process walkthrough, can the learner produce an accurate as-is BPMN diagram of it?
concepts.practice_objective: Convert a described current process into an as-is BPMN diagram.
concepts.central_mental_model: An as-is model documents reality first, before anyone proposes changing it.

toc_location.tile_summary: Learn BPMN 2.0 core notation, then model an existing (as-is) process and a redesigned (to-be) process.

concepts.primary_objective: Model a proposed (to-be) business process in BPMN reflecting a redesigned future state.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an as-is model and a set of proposed changes, can the learner produce a to-be BPMN diagram reflecting them?
concepts.practice_objective: Redesign a given as-is BPMN diagram into a to-be diagram implementing 2 stated changes.
concepts.central_mental_model: A to-be model is a design artifact: the process as it should work, not as it does.

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify gaps and bottlenecks between as-is and to-be process models and apply process improvement techniques.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify gaps and bottlenecks by comparing as-is and to-be process models or examining process flow.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an as-is diagram, can the learner locate the bottleneck step(s) and justify the choice?
concepts.practice_objective: Annotate a given as-is diagram to mark its bottleneck and the gap versus the to-be version.
concepts.central_mental_model: A bottleneck is the step that caps the whole process's throughput; finding it is the point of the comparison.

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify gaps and bottlenecks between as-is and to-be process models and apply process improvement techniques.

concepts.primary_objective: Apply process improvement techniques (e.g. Lean waste elimination) to redesign a process for efficiency.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an identified bottleneck, can the learner propose a specific, justified process improvement?
concepts.practice_objective: Propose one process-improvement change for a given bottleneck and justify its expected effect.
concepts.central_mental_model: Process improvement is targeted redesign aimed at a diagnosed inefficiency, not general tidying.

toc_location.tile_summary: Document business rules and represent decision logic using decision tables and decision trees.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Decision Model and Notation, a companion OMG standard to BPMN mentioned by name as related tooling, not taught here.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify and document business rules (constraints/policies) that govern process or system behavior.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a process description, can the learner extract and state the implicit business rules governing it?
concepts.practice_objective: Extract 3 business rules implied by a described approval process.
concepts.central_mental_model: Business rules are the underlying policies and constraints that produce a process's observed behavior -- they explain WHY a process branches the way it does, separate from the process flow diagram itself.

toc_location.tile_summary: Document business rules and represent decision logic using decision tables and decision trees.

concepts.primary_objective: Build a decision table that maps combinations of condition values to the correct action/outcome.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a set of rules with multiple conditions, can the learner build a complete, non-contradictory decision table?
concepts.practice_objective: Convert 3 written business rules with 2 conditions each into a decision table.
concepts.central_mental_model: A decision table lists every combination of condition values in rows, mapping each combination to exactly one action -- forcing completeness and catching contradictions that prose rule descriptions hide.

toc_location.tile_summary: Document business rules and represent decision logic using decision tables and decision trees.

concepts.primary_objective: Build a decision tree that represents sequential branching logic for a decision with ordered conditions.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a set of sequential rules, can the learner build a decision tree with correctly ordered branches?
concepts.practice_objective: Convert a described sequential eligibility rule into a decision tree diagram.
concepts.central_mental_model: A decision tree represents rules as ordered, sequential branches evaluated one after another -- suited to decisions where conditions are naturally checked in a specific order, unlike a decision table's all-at-once combination view.

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify entities and attributes from a business narrative, then identify primary keys and enforce referential integrity with foreign keys.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify the entities and their attributes relevant to a business domain from a narrative description.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a business narrative, can the learner list the correct entities and attributes it implies?
concepts.practice_objective: Extract the entities and 3 attributes each from a given business narrative.
concepts.central_mental_model: An entity is a distinct thing worth tracking; attributes are the facts you record about it.

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify entities and attributes from a business narrative, then identify primary keys and enforce referential integrity with foreign keys.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify the column(s) that uniquely identify each row of a table.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a table's columns, can the learner identify a valid primary key?
concepts.practice_objective: Select a valid primary key for 3 given sample tables.
concepts.central_mental_model: A primary key is the guarantee that every row can be uniquely and stably addressed.

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify entities and attributes from a business narrative, then identify primary keys and enforce referential integrity with foreign keys.

concepts.primary_objective: Use a foreign key to reference another table's primary key and maintain referential integrity.
concepts.assessment_target: Given two related tables, can the learner identify the correct foreign key and a referential-integrity violation?
concepts.practice_objective: Identify the foreign key linking 2 given tables and spot a referential-integrity violation in sample data.
concepts.central_mental_model: A foreign key is a pointer that must always resolve to a real row, or the data becomes inconsistent.

toc_location.tile_summary: Model one-to-many and many-to-many relationships, including junction tables, and determine relationship cardinality.

concepts.primary_objective: Recognize and model a one-to-many relationship between two entities.
concepts.assessment_target: Given two entities, can the learner determine whether their relationship is one-to-many and model it correctly?
concepts.practice_objective: Model a one-to-many relationship for a given entity pair (e.g. customer-orders).
concepts.central_mental_model: A one-to-many relationship means one row on one side can relate to many rows on the other, never the reverse.

toc_location.tile_summary: Model one-to-many and many-to-many relationships, including junction tables, and determine relationship cardinality.

concepts.primary_objective: Recognize a many-to-many relationship and resolve it with a junction/bridge table.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a many-to-many scenario, can the learner design the correct junction table with both foreign keys?
concepts.practice_objective: Design a junction table resolving a given many-to-many scenario (e.g. students-courses).
concepts.central_mental_model: A relational table can't directly represent many-to-many; a junction table breaks it into two one-to-many relationships.

toc_location.tile_summary: Model one-to-many and many-to-many relationships, including junction tables, and determine relationship cardinality.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A common visual convention for showing cardinality on an ERD-style diagram, introduced here as the notation used to draw the cardinality determined in this concept.

concepts.primary_objective: Determine and notate the cardinality (one-to-many, many-to-many) of a relationship between two entities using crow's-foot notation.
concepts.assessment_target: Given two related entities whose relationship is one-to-many or many-to-many, can the learner determine and correctly notate their cardinality?
concepts.practice_objective: Determine and draw the cardinality between 2 given entity pairs (one-to-many or many-to-many) using crow's-foot notation.
concepts.central_mental_model: Cardinality notation states how many of one entity can relate to how many of another.

toc_location.tile_title: Diagramming and Applying the Data Model
toc_location.tile_summary: Draw an entity-relationship diagram, distinguish conceptual from logical data models, and map business information needs to the model.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A common visual convention for showing cardinality on an ERD, mentioned as the typical notation style used in examples.

concepts.primary_objective: Draw an entity-relationship diagram representing entities, attributes, and relationships for a business domain.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a business scenario, can the learner produce a correct ERD with entities, key attributes, and relationships?
concepts.practice_objective: Draw an ERD for a simple described business scenario (e.g. orders and customers).
concepts.central_mental_model: An ERD is a visual notation for a conceptual data model, independent of any particular database engine.

toc_location.tile_title: Diagramming and Applying the Data Model
toc_location.tile_summary: Draw an entity-relationship diagram, distinguish conceptual from logical data models, and map business information needs to the model.

concepts.primary_objective: Distinguish a conceptual data model (business language, no implementation detail) from a logical data model (typed, normalized, implementation-ready).
concepts.assessment_target: Given a data model artifact, can the learner classify it as conceptual or logical and justify the classification?
concepts.practice_objective: Classify 3 given data model excerpts as conceptual or logical and state the distinguishing detail.
concepts.central_mental_model: Conceptual and logical models sit at different abstraction levels: business meaning versus implementation-ready structure.

toc_location.tile_title: Diagramming and Applying the Data Model
toc_location.tile_summary: Draw an entity-relationship diagram, distinguish conceptual from logical data models, and map business information needs to the model.

concepts.primary_objective: Map a stakeholder's business information needs to the data entities/attributes that would satisfy them.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a stated business question, can the learner map it to the entities/attributes needed to answer it?
concepts.practice_objective: Map a given business question (e.g. 'which customers churned') to the entities/attributes required to answer it.
concepts.central_mental_model: Data modeling starts from what business questions must be answerable, not from the data that happens to exist.

toc_location.tile_title: Relational Model, SELECT, and Inner Join
toc_location.tile_summary: Understand the relational model, write SELECT statements, and combine matching rows from two tables with an INNER JOIN.

concepts.primary_objective: Understand that relational data is organized into tables of rows and columns, each table modeling one entity type.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a dataset, can the learner identify which table each fact belongs in under the relational model?
concepts.practice_objective: Sort a mixed set of facts into the correct table for a given simple schema.
concepts.central_mental_model: The relational model organizes data as independent tables joined by shared keys, not one flat sheet.

toc_location.tile_title: Relational Model, SELECT, and Inner Join
toc_location.tile_summary: Understand the relational model, write SELECT statements, and combine matching rows from two tables with an INNER JOIN.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The specific SQL dialect used for examples in this path per its version scope, mentioned as the reference environment, not a separate taught topic.

concepts.primary_objective: Write a SQL SELECT statement to retrieve specific columns and rows from a table.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a data need, can the learner write a correct SELECT statement returning exactly the required columns?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a SELECT statement retrieving 3 named columns from a given table.
concepts.central_mental_model: SELECT names which columns and rows of a table you want back, nothing more.

toc_location.tile_title: Relational Model, SELECT, and Inner Join
toc_location.tile_summary: Understand the relational model, write SELECT statements, and combine matching rows from two tables with an INNER JOIN.

concepts.primary_objective: Combine matching rows from two tables on a shared key using INNER JOIN.
concepts.assessment_target: Given two related tables, can the learner write an INNER JOIN returning only matched rows?
concepts.practice_objective: Write an INNER JOIN combining 2 given tables on their shared key.
concepts.central_mental_model: INNER JOIN keeps only rows that have a match on both sides of the key.

toc_location.tile_summary: Aggregate rows with GROUP BY, filter with WHERE and HAVING, and choose data types while handling NULL values.

concepts.primary_objective: Aggregate rows into summary groups using GROUP BY with aggregate functions (SUM, COUNT, AVG).
concepts.assessment_target: Given a raw table, can the learner write a GROUP BY query producing correct per-group aggregates?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a query grouping a given table by one column and summing another.
concepts.central_mental_model: GROUP BY collapses many rows into one summary row per distinct group value.

concepts.concept_name: SQL Filtering with WHERE and HAVING

toc_location.tile_summary: Aggregate rows with GROUP BY, filter with WHERE and HAVING, and choose data types while handling NULL values.

concepts.primary_objective: Filter rows before aggregation with WHERE and filter grouped results after aggregation with HAVING.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a filtering requirement on raw vs. aggregated data, can the learner choose WHERE vs HAVING correctly?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a query using WHERE to filter raw rows and HAVING to filter an aggregate result.
concepts.central_mental_model: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation -- different filtering stages.

concepts.concept_name: SQL Data Types and NULL Handling

toc_location.tile_summary: Aggregate rows with GROUP BY, filter with WHERE and HAVING, and choose data types while handling NULL values.

inline_vocabulary.definition: SQL's marker for a missing or unknown value, introduced inline as the specific keyword this concept covers.

concepts.primary_objective: Choose appropriate SQL data types for columns and handle NULL (unknown/missing) values correctly in queries.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a query with NULLs, can the learner predict its behavior and use IS NULL/COALESCE correctly?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a query that correctly filters or substitutes NULL values using IS NULL and COALESCE.
concepts.central_mental_model: NULL means unknown, not zero or empty, and comparisons against NULL never evaluate true.

toc_location.tile_summary: Combine tables with LEFT, RIGHT, and FULL OUTER JOIN to preserve unmatched rows from either or both sides.

concepts.primary_objective: Combine two tables with LEFT OUTER JOIN, keeping all left-table rows even without a match.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a scenario needing unmatched left rows preserved, can the learner write the correct LEFT JOIN?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a LEFT JOIN that preserves unmatched rows from a given left table.
concepts.central_mental_model: LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table, filling unmatched right-side columns with NULL.

toc_location.tile_summary: Combine tables with LEFT, RIGHT, and FULL OUTER JOIN to preserve unmatched rows from either or both sides.

concepts.primary_objective: Combine two tables with RIGHT OUTER JOIN, keeping all right-table rows even without a match.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a scenario needing unmatched right rows preserved, can the learner write the correct RIGHT JOIN?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a RIGHT JOIN that preserves unmatched rows from a given right table.
concepts.central_mental_model: RIGHT JOIN mirrors LEFT JOIN, preserving the right table's unmatched rows instead.

toc_location.tile_summary: Combine tables with LEFT, RIGHT, and FULL OUTER JOIN to preserve unmatched rows from either or both sides.

concepts.primary_objective: Combine two tables with FULL OUTER JOIN, keeping unmatched rows from both sides.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a scenario needing all rows from both tables regardless of match, can the learner write a FULL OUTER JOIN?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a FULL OUTER JOIN retaining unmatched rows from both given tables.
concepts.central_mental_model: FULL OUTER JOIN unions the unmatched rows of both LEFT and RIGHT joins.

toc_location.tile_summary: Sort query results with ORDER BY and apply common business-reporting query patterns such as period-over-period comparisons.

concepts.primary_objective: Sort query results using ORDER BY, ascending or descending, on one or more columns.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a sorting requirement, can the learner write ORDER BY with the correct column(s) and direction?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a query sorting a given table by two columns, one ascending one descending.
concepts.central_mental_model: ORDER BY only controls display sequence; it doesn't change which rows are returned.

toc_location.tile_summary: Sort query results with ORDER BY and apply common business-reporting query patterns such as period-over-period comparisons.

concepts.primary_objective: Write SQL queries following common business-reporting patterns (e.g. period-over-period, top-N, running totals) to answer reporting questions.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a business reporting question, can the learner compose a query using the right query pattern?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a query answering a given business reporting question (e.g. top 5 customers by revenue).
concepts.central_mental_model: Business reporting queries recur in a small set of patterns that map directly onto common business questions.

concepts.concept_name: Power BI Data Import and Transformation

toc_location.tile_title: Connecting Power BI and Tableau to Data
toc_location.tile_summary: Import and transform data into Power BI with Power Query, and connect Tableau to a data source and prepare it for dashboards.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Baseline familiarity with launching Power BI Desktop and its general layout -- informal tool-orientation exposure, not formally taught as a separate concept.

concepts.primary_objective: Import and transform data into Power BI using Power Query (Get Data, shape, clean).
concepts.assessment_target: Given a raw data source, can the learner import it and apply the transformation steps needed to make it report-ready?
concepts.practice_objective: Import a given raw dataset into Power BI and apply 2 Power Query transformation steps.
concepts.central_mental_model: Power Query is a repeatable transform pipeline applied once at import so downstream reports see clean data.

toc_location.tile_title: Connecting Power BI and Tableau to Data
toc_location.tile_summary: Import and transform data into Power BI with Power Query, and connect Tableau to a data source and prepare it for dashboards.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Baseline familiarity with launching Tableau Desktop and its general layout -- informal tool-orientation exposure, not formally taught as a separate concept.

concepts.primary_objective: Connect Tableau to a data source and prepare it (joins, extracts) for use in dashboards.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a raw data source, can the learner connect Tableau to it and prepare the needed extract/join?
concepts.practice_objective: Connect Tableau to a given data source and configure one join or extract.
concepts.central_mental_model: Tableau's data connection step prepares raw data into a queryable source before any visual is built.

toc_location.tile_title: Assessing Current State, Future State, and Gaps
toc_location.tile_summary: Assess the current state, define a future-state vision, identify the gap between them, and conduct a SWOT analysis.

concepts.primary_objective: Assess an organization's current business capability/state as a baseline before proposing change.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a business area description, can the learner produce a structured current-state capability assessment?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a current-state capability assessment for a given business area.
concepts.central_mental_model: You can't measure a gap without first honestly baselining where things stand today.

toc_location.tile_title: Assessing Current State, Future State, and Gaps
toc_location.tile_summary: Assess the current state, define a future-state vision, identify the gap between them, and conduct a SWOT analysis.

concepts.primary_objective: Define a future-state vision describing the desired target state an initiative should achieve.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a business goal, can the learner write a concrete, measurable future-state vision statement?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a future-state vision statement for a given business goal.
concepts.central_mental_model: A future-state vision is a concrete destination, not an aspiration -- specific enough to plan toward.

toc_location.tile_title: Assessing Current State, Future State, and Gaps
toc_location.tile_summary: Assess the current state, define a future-state vision, identify the gap between them, and conduct a SWOT analysis.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify the gap between current state and future state and articulate what must change to close it.
concepts.assessment_target: Given current-state and future-state descriptions, can the learner identify the specific gaps between them?
concepts.practice_objective: Compare given current- and future-state descriptions and list the concrete gaps.
concepts.central_mental_model: The gap is the delta between where things are and where they need to be -- the actual work to be done.

toc_location.tile_title: Assessing Current State, Future State, and Gaps
toc_location.tile_summary: Assess the current state, define a future-state vision, identify the gap between them, and conduct a SWOT analysis.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats -- the well-known four-quadrant framework this concept applies, spelled out only as the acronym expansion.

concepts.primary_objective: Conduct a SWOT analysis identifying strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats for a business situation.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a business scenario, can the learner correctly categorize factors into the 4 SWOT quadrants?
concepts.practice_objective: Build a SWOT matrix for a given business scenario.
concepts.central_mental_model: SWOT splits factors along two axes: internal-vs-external and helpful-vs-harmful.

toc_location.tile_summary: Prioritize requirements using MoSCoW categories, the Kano model, and a weighted scoring model.

concepts.primary_objective: Prioritize requirements using MoSCoW categories: Must, Should, Could, Won't have.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a requirements list, can the learner assign a justified MoSCoW category to each?
concepts.practice_objective: Categorize 8 given requirements into Must/Should/Could/Won't.
concepts.central_mental_model: MoSCoW forces an explicit trade-off decision on every requirement instead of leaving priority implicit.

toc_location.tile_summary: Prioritize requirements using MoSCoW categories, the Kano model, and a weighted scoring model.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Named after Noriaki Kano, whose satisfaction-vs-functionality framework this concept applies; the name is mentioned as attribution, not as separate biographical content.

concepts.primary_objective: Classify features using the Kano model (basic, performance, delighter) to understand their effect on satisfaction.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a feature list, can the learner classify each into the correct Kano category and justify it?
concepts.practice_objective: Classify 5 given features into Kano categories with justification.
concepts.central_mental_model: Kano shows satisfaction isn't linear with investment -- some features only prevent dissatisfaction, others create delight.

toc_location.tile_summary: Prioritize requirements using MoSCoW categories, the Kano model, and a weighted scoring model.

concepts.primary_objective: Build a weighted scoring model that ranks requirements/options by weighted criteria totals.
concepts.assessment_target: Given criteria with weights and options, can the learner compute correct weighted scores and rank the options?
concepts.practice_objective: Score 4 given options against 3 weighted criteria and rank the results.
concepts.central_mental_model: Weighted scoring converts multiple criteria of different importance into one comparable number per option.

toc_location.tile_title: Evaluating Solutions and Building the Business Case
toc_location.tile_summary: Evaluate candidate solutions, develop a business case, and apply multi-criteria decision analysis to compare options.

concepts.primary_objective: Evaluate multiple candidate solutions/vendors against defined criteria and recommend the best fit.
concepts.assessment_target: Given 2-3 candidate solutions and criteria, can the learner score them and justify a recommendation?
concepts.practice_objective: Score 2 candidate solutions against 3 given criteria and recommend one.
concepts.central_mental_model: Solution evaluation compares options against explicit criteria so the choice is defensible, not just preferred.

toc_location.tile_title: Evaluating Solutions and Building the Business Case
toc_location.tile_summary: Evaluate candidate solutions, develop a business case, and apply multi-criteria decision analysis to compare options.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Return on Investment -- the ratio of expected benefit to cost used as one standard justification metric within a business case, spelled out only as the acronym expansion.

concepts.primary_objective: Develop a business case with cost-benefit analysis justifying a proposed initiative.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a proposed initiative, can the learner build a business case with quantified costs, benefits, and a recommendation?
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a business case (costs, benefits, ROI, recommendation) for a given proposed initiative.
concepts.central_mental_model: A business case is the financial and strategic argument for why an initiative deserves funding.

toc_location.tile_title: Evaluating Solutions and Building the Business Case
toc_location.tile_summary: Evaluate candidate solutions, develop a business case, and apply multi-criteria decision analysis to compare options.

concepts.primary_objective: Apply multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) to compare options against several non-comparable dimensions systematically.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a multi-dimensional decision scenario, can the learner apply an MCDA method to reach a defensible ranking?
concepts.practice_objective: Apply an MCDA method to rank 3 options across 3 non-comparable criteria.
concepts.central_mental_model: MCDA gives a structured method for comparing options when criteria can't be reduced to one common unit.

toc_location.tile_summary: Compute mean, median, and mode, plus range, variance, and standard deviation, to describe a dataset.

concepts.primary_objective: Compute and choose among mean, median, and mode to describe a dataset's central tendency.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a dataset, can the learner compute all three measures and choose the most appropriate one, with justification?
concepts.practice_objective: Compute mean, median, and mode for a given dataset and justify which best represents it.
concepts.central_mental_model: Mean, median, and mode each answer 'what's typical' differently, and outliers/skew determine which is honest.

toc_location.tile_summary: Compute mean, median, and mode, plus range, variance, and standard deviation, to describe a dataset.

concepts.primary_objective: Compute and interpret range, variance, and standard deviation to describe a dataset's spread.
concepts.assessment_target: Given two datasets with similar centers but different spreads, can the learner compute and interpret the difference?
concepts.practice_objective: Compute range and standard deviation for a given dataset and interpret what it says about consistency.
concepts.central_mental_model: A measure of center alone hides how consistent or variable the underlying data actually is.

toc_location.tile_summary: Write and refine user stories, then maintain and groom a product backlog.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The mnemonic checklist (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable) this concept applies to judge whether a user story is well-formed, spelled out only as the acronym expansion.

concepts.primary_objective: Write and refine user stories following INVEST criteria, including splitting oversized stories.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a large/vague story, can the learner rewrite or split it to satisfy INVEST criteria?
concepts.practice_objective: Split a given oversized user story into 2-3 INVEST-compliant stories.
concepts.central_mental_model: INVEST is the checklist for whether a story is small and clear enough to actually be plannable and testable.

toc_location.tile_summary: Write and refine user stories, then maintain and groom a product backlog.

concepts.primary_objective: Maintain and groom a product backlog: ordering, refining, and keeping items ready for upcoming sprints.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a messy backlog, can the learner reorder and refine it into a sprint-ready state?
concepts.practice_objective: Groom a given messy backlog: reorder, split oversized items, and mark refinement status.
concepts.central_mental_model: Backlog management keeps a living, ordered list where the top is always refined enough to pull into a sprint.

toc_location.tile_summary: Sequence prioritized requirements into delivery phases and collaboratively define testable acceptance criteria for backlog items.

concepts.primary_objective: Sequence prioritized requirements into delivery phases/releases based on priority, dependency, and capacity.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a prioritized backlog, can the learner sequence it into sensible releases respecting dependencies?
concepts.practice_objective: Sequence 10 prioritized requirements into 3 releases, respecting given dependencies.
concepts.central_mental_model: Phased delivery turns a priority-ordered list into a realistic release plan bounded by capacity and dependency.

toc_location.tile_summary: Sequence prioritized requirements into delivery phases and collaboratively define testable acceptance criteria for backlog items.

concepts.primary_objective: Collaboratively define testable acceptance criteria for a backlog item during refinement, establishing what 'done' means.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a backlog item, can the learner define acceptance criteria that are specific, testable, and negotiated with the team?
concepts.practice_objective: Facilitate defining acceptance criteria for a given backlog item in a mock refinement discussion.
concepts.central_mental_model: Acceptance criteria are the negotiated, testable boundary of 'done' agreed before work starts, not written solo after.

toc_location.tile_summary: Write clear business reports, adapt content for technical and non-technical audiences, deliver stakeholder presentations, and run requirements walkthroughs for sign-off.

concepts.primary_objective: Write a clear business report/executive summary that communicates analysis findings to a business audience.
concepts.assessment_target: Given raw findings, can the learner write a structured, audience-appropriate written report or executive summary?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a one-page executive summary from a given set of raw analysis findings.
concepts.central_mental_model: A business report leads with the conclusion and supports it, rather than narrating the analysis chronologically.

concepts.concept_name: Communicating to Technical vs Non-Technical Audiences

toc_location.tile_summary: Write clear business reports, adapt content for technical and non-technical audiences, deliver stakeholder presentations, and run requirements walkthroughs for sign-off.

concepts.primary_objective: Adapt the same technical content for both technical and non-technical audiences without changing its meaning.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a technical statement, can the learner rewrite it accurately for a non-technical audience?
concepts.practice_objective: Rewrite a given technical requirement for a non-technical stakeholder audience, preserving its meaning.
concepts.central_mental_model: The same fact needs different vocabulary and framing depending on the audience's technical fluency.

toc_location.tile_summary: Write clear business reports, adapt content for technical and non-technical audiences, deliver stakeholder presentations, and run requirements walkthroughs for sign-off.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A colloquial term for a very short, high-level summary of findings, mentioned in passing as one presentation style.

concepts.primary_objective: Design and deliver a stakeholder presentation/slide deck communicating analysis or recommendations.
concepts.assessment_target: Given findings, can the learner structure a presentation deck appropriately for a stakeholder audience?
concepts.practice_objective: Outline a 5-slide stakeholder presentation from given findings.
concepts.central_mental_model: A presentation deck structures the same content as a report differently, for a live, time-boxed audience.

toc_location.tile_summary: Write clear business reports, adapt content for technical and non-technical audiences, deliver stakeholder presentations, and run requirements walkthroughs for sign-off.

concepts.primary_objective: Run a requirements walkthrough/demo session to review requirements and obtain sign-off from stakeholders.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a requirements set, can the learner plan a walkthrough session that secures explicit stakeholder sign-off?
concepts.practice_objective: Plan a requirements walkthrough agenda for a given requirements set, including a sign-off step.
concepts.central_mental_model: A walkthrough converts a written requirement into a shared, witnessed agreement via live review.

toc_location.tile_summary: Draw a scope/context diagram showing a system's boundary, then break down a business function into a hierarchy of sub-functions.

concepts.primary_objective: Draw a scope/context diagram showing a system's boundary and its external actors/interfaces.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a system description, can the learner draw a correct context diagram with system boundary and external entities?
concepts.practice_objective: Draw a context diagram for a given system description.
concepts.central_mental_model: A context diagram fixes what's inside versus outside the system boundary before any internal detail is modeled.

toc_location.tile_summary: Draw a scope/context diagram showing a system's boundary, then break down a business function into a hierarchy of sub-functions.

concepts.primary_objective: Break down a business function into a hierarchy of sub-functions via functional decomposition.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a top-level function, can the learner decompose it into a correct sub-function hierarchy?
concepts.practice_objective: Decompose a given top-level business function into 2 levels of sub-functions.
concepts.central_mental_model: Functional decomposition breaks a large function into smaller, independently understandable pieces top-down.

toc_location.tile_summary: Use cell references and basic formulas, build pivot tables, and use lookup functions to retrieve values across tables.

concepts.primary_objective: Use relative and absolute cell references and basic formulas (SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT) in a spreadsheet.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a formula-copy scenario, can the learner correctly apply relative vs absolute references and basic aggregate functions?
concepts.practice_objective: Write and correctly copy a formula using both relative and absolute references across a range.
concepts.central_mental_model: A relative reference shifts when copied; an absolute reference (with $) stays fixed -- the difference determines correctness when copying formulas.

toc_location.tile_summary: Use cell references and basic formulas, build pivot tables, and use lookup functions to retrieve values across tables.

concepts.primary_objective: Build a pivot table to summarize and cross-tabulate raw spreadsheet data.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a raw data table, can the learner build a pivot table answering a specific summary question?
concepts.practice_objective: Build a pivot table from a given dataset answering a specific summary question.
concepts.central_mental_model: A pivot table reshapes raw rows into a cross-tabulated summary without altering the source data.

toc_location.tile_summary: Use cell references and basic formulas, build pivot tables, and use lookup functions to retrieve values across tables.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A specific Excel lookup function named as one example of the lookup-function family this concept covers.
A newer Excel lookup function named as another example of the lookup-function family this concept covers.

concepts.primary_objective: Use lookup functions (VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH) to retrieve a value from another table based on a key match.
concepts.assessment_target: Given two related tables, can the learner write a correct lookup formula pulling the right value?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a lookup formula pulling a value from a second table based on a shared key.
concepts.central_mental_model: A lookup formula finds a matching key in one table and returns a corresponding value from it.

toc_location.tile_title: Conditional Logic, Visualization, and Ad Hoc Reporting
toc_location.tile_summary: Write conditional formulas, build charts to visualize data, and produce a quick ad hoc business analysis report.

concepts.primary_objective: Write conditional formulas (IF, nested IF, IFS) that return different results based on a condition.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a business rule, can the learner encode it as a correct conditional formula?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a conditional formula implementing a given 3-branch business rule.
concepts.central_mental_model: A conditional formula encodes an if/then business rule directly into a cell's calculation.

toc_location.tile_title: Conditional Logic, Visualization, and Ad Hoc Reporting
toc_location.tile_summary: Write conditional formulas, build charts to visualize data, and produce a quick ad hoc business analysis report.

concepts.primary_objective: Build a chart in a spreadsheet that correctly visualizes a given dataset and question.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a dataset and a question, can the learner choose the right chart type and build it correctly?
concepts.practice_objective: Build a chart in a spreadsheet answering a given question about a dataset.
concepts.central_mental_model: Chart choice should match the question being asked of the data, not just what looks appealing.

toc_location.tile_title: Conditional Logic, Visualization, and Ad Hoc Reporting
toc_location.tile_summary: Write conditional formulas, build charts to visualize data, and produce a quick ad hoc business analysis report.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Excel's chart type built directly from a pivot table, mentioned in passing as an output format for ad hoc reports.

concepts.primary_objective: Produce a quick, one-off business analysis report in a spreadsheet in response to an ad hoc stakeholder request.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an ad hoc data question, can the learner produce a fast, correct spreadsheet-based answer with minimal formal process?
concepts.practice_objective: Produce a one-page ad hoc analysis answering a given stakeholder data question using a spreadsheet.
concepts.central_mental_model: Ad hoc reporting favors speed and directness over the formality of a scheduled/published report.

toc_location.tile_summary: Participate in sprint planning, clarifying requirements and acceptance criteria, and collaborate with the Product Owner and delivery team.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The specific agile framework whose ceremony names (sprint, standup, retrospective) this concept and its siblings use, named as context, not taught as a full framework.

concepts.primary_objective: Participate in sprint planning as a BA: clarifying requirements and acceptance criteria so the team can commit to a sprint's scope.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a candidate sprint backlog, can the learner identify which items lack sufficient clarity for the team to commit to?
concepts.practice_objective: Review a candidate sprint backlog and flag items needing more clarification before commitment.
concepts.central_mental_model: Sprint planning is where the team commits to a scope of work for the sprint -- the BA's job is ensuring every item the team is about to commit to is actually clear enough to build, not just clear enough to sound plausible in a meeting.

toc_location.tile_summary: Participate in sprint planning, clarifying requirements and acceptance criteria, and collaborate with the Product Owner and delivery team.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The Scrum role a BA collaborates with when refining and prioritizing backlog items, named as the counterpart role, not taught as a role definition.

concepts.primary_objective: Collaborate effectively as a BA with the Product Owner and delivery team across the sprint cycle.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a BA/PO role-ambiguity scenario, can the learner identify the correct collaboration boundary and action?
concepts.practice_objective: Resolve a given BA/PO role-ambiguity scenario by proposing the correct collaboration approach.
concepts.central_mental_model: BA and PO roles overlap in agile teams; effective collaboration requires an explicit, negotiated division of labor.

toc_location.tile_summary: Participate in the daily standup, sprint review, and sprint retrospective as a BA.

concepts.primary_objective: Participate in the daily standup as a BA, surfacing blockers relevant to requirements/clarification without turning it into a status meeting.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a standup update, can the learner distinguish an appropriate blocker-surfacing update from an inappropriate detailed status report?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a standup-appropriate (blocker-focused) update for a given BA work-in-progress scenario.
concepts.central_mental_model: The daily standup exists to surface blockers fast, not to deliver detailed status -- a BA's update should be blocker-focused and brief, since a long status report defeats the ceremony's purpose.

toc_location.tile_summary: Participate in the daily standup, sprint review, and sprint retrospective as a BA.

concepts.primary_objective: Participate in sprint review as a BA, helping validate delivered work against acceptance criteria with stakeholders.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a demoed increment, can the learner check it against its original acceptance criteria and flag a mismatch?
concepts.practice_objective: Check a given demoed feature against its acceptance criteria and flag any mismatch.
concepts.central_mental_model: Sprint review closes the loop between what was committed to and what was delivered -- the BA checks the demoed increment against the acceptance criteria agreed on during refinement, not against a new, informal judgment of 'does this look right.'

toc_location.tile_summary: Participate in the daily standup, sprint review, and sprint retrospective as a BA.

concepts.primary_objective: Participate in a sprint retrospective as a BA, contributing to identifying process improvements for the team.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a sprint's events, can the learner identify a specific, actionable process-improvement item for the retrospective?
concepts.practice_objective: Propose one actionable improvement item from a given sprint's described events.
concepts.central_mental_model: The retrospective looks backward at the team's process, not the product -- its output is one concrete, actionable process improvement, not a re-litigation of individual story outcomes.

toc_location.tile_summary: Apply the Five Whys technique and build a fishbone diagram to trace a problem to its root cause.

concepts.primary_objective: Apply the Five Whys technique to trace a problem back to its root cause by repeatedly asking why.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a symptom, can the learner apply Five Whys correctly to reach a root cause distinct from the symptom?
concepts.practice_objective: Apply Five Whys to a given problem symptom to reach and state its root cause.
concepts.central_mental_model: Repeatedly asking 'why' peels back layers of a symptom one cause at a time until a true root cause is reached -- stopping at the first answer usually just restates the symptom, not its cause.

toc_location.tile_summary: Apply the Five Whys technique and build a fishbone diagram to trace a problem to its root cause.

concepts.primary_objective: Build a fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram organizing candidate causes of a problem into standard categories.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a problem, can the learner build a fishbone diagram sorting candidate causes into appropriate categories?
concepts.practice_objective: Build a fishbone diagram for a given problem with causes sorted into at least 3 categories.
concepts.central_mental_model: A fishbone diagram sorts brainstormed candidate causes into standard categories (e.g. people, process, tools, environment) branching off a central problem, making it easier to see which cause areas are under- or over-represented.

toc_location.tile_summary: Define and apply a Definition of Done as the team-wide quality bar every backlog item must meet.

concepts.primary_objective: Define and apply a Definition of Done (DoD) as the team-wide quality bar every backlog item must meet before being called complete.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a completed item, can the learner check it against a DoD checklist and correctly flag a failing criterion?
concepts.practice_objective: Check a given completed item against a 5-point DoD checklist and flag any failure.
concepts.central_mental_model: DoD is a team-wide, item-independent quality bar, distinct from an item-specific acceptance criterion.

concepts.concept_name: Star Schema / Dimensional Modeling for BI

toc_location.tile_title: Star Schema and Data Model Relationships
toc_location.tile_summary: Design a star schema of fact and dimension tables, then define relationships between tables so visuals can query across them.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The central table of measurable events in a star schema, introduced inline as vocabulary for describing the schema shape.
A descriptive, lookup-style table that surrounds a fact table in a star schema, introduced inline as vocabulary for describing the schema shape.

concepts.primary_objective: Design a star schema (fact and dimension tables) for a BI data model to support efficient analytical queries.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a business process to report on, can the learner design a correct fact table and its surrounding dimension tables?
concepts.practice_objective: Design a star schema (1 fact table, 3 dimension tables) for a given business process.
concepts.central_mental_model: A star schema separates numeric facts from descriptive dimensions so analytical queries stay simple and fast.

concepts.concept_name: Data Model Relationships in BI Tools

toc_location.tile_title: Star Schema and Data Model Relationships
toc_location.tile_summary: Design a star schema of fact and dimension tables, then define relationships between tables so visuals can query across them.

concepts.primary_objective: Define relationships between tables within a BI tool's data model so visuals can query across them correctly.
concepts.assessment_target: Given multiple imported tables, can the learner set up correct relationships in the BI tool's model view?
concepts.practice_objective: Configure relationships between 2 imported tables in a BI tool's model view.
concepts.central_mental_model: A BI tool's relationships let visuals pull fields from multiple tables as if they were one, without duplicating data.

toc_location.tile_title: Designing Power BI and Tableau Dashboards
toc_location.tile_summary: Design a Power BI dashboard and a Tableau dashboard, each laying out visuals to answer a stakeholder's reporting needs.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Power BI's data-shaping editor, named in passing as the tool used before report design, not itself taught as a separate concept in this path.

concepts.primary_objective: Design a Power BI dashboard/report page laying out visuals to answer a stakeholder's reporting needs.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a reporting requirement, can the learner design a Power BI report page with appropriate visuals and layout?
concepts.practice_objective: Design a one-page Power BI report layout for a given stakeholder reporting need.
concepts.central_mental_model: Dashboard design is choosing and arranging visuals so a viewer can answer their question at a glance.

toc_location.tile_title: Designing Power BI and Tableau Dashboards
toc_location.tile_summary: Design a Power BI dashboard and a Tableau dashboard, each laying out visuals to answer a stakeholder's reporting needs.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The specific Tableau product edition used for examples per this path's version scope, mentioned as the reference environment.

concepts.primary_objective: Design a Tableau dashboard laying out visuals to answer a stakeholder's reporting needs.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a reporting requirement, can the learner design a Tableau dashboard with appropriate visuals and layout?
concepts.practice_objective: Design a one-page Tableau dashboard layout for a given stakeholder reporting need.
concepts.central_mental_model: Tableau dashboard design applies the same visual-communication goal as Power BI, within Tableau's authoring model.

toc_location.tile_summary: Apply visual design principles to declutter and improve dashboards, then publish and share the finished report with stakeholders.

concepts.primary_objective: Apply visual design principles (chart selection, layout, color, decluttering) to make dashboards readable and accurate.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a poorly designed chart, can the learner identify and fix its visual design flaw?
concepts.practice_objective: Redesign a given cluttered/misleading chart applying 2 visual design principles.
concepts.central_mental_model: A chart's visual design should make the intended comparison obvious at a glance, not just display the data.

toc_location.tile_summary: Apply visual design principles to declutter and improve dashboards, then publish and share the finished report with stakeholders.

concepts.primary_objective: Publish and share a finished BI report/dashboard with stakeholders through the appropriate delivery mechanism (e.g. Power BI Service).
concepts.assessment_target: Given a finished report and an audience, can the learner choose and execute the correct sharing/permissions setup?
concepts.practice_objective: Publish a given report and configure sharing/permissions for a named stakeholder audience.
concepts.central_mental_model: Delivery is a distinct final step: a finished report has no value until the right audience can access it.

concepts.concept_name: Power BI Measures and Calculated Columns (DAX)

toc_location.tile_title: DAX, Calculated Fields, and the Semantic Layer
toc_location.tile_summary: Write DAX measures in Power BI and calculated fields in Tableau, then build a centralized semantic layer that shares metric definitions across reports.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Data Analysis Expressions, Power BI's formula language; named as the language measures are written in, mentioned in passing rather than taught as general-purpose programming.

concepts.primary_objective: Write DAX measures and calculated columns in Power BI to compute business metrics.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a metric requirement, can the learner write a correct DAX measure (and distinguish it from a calculated column)?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a DAX measure computing a given business metric (e.g. year-over-year growth).
concepts.central_mental_model: A DAX measure recalculates dynamically based on the current filter/slicer context at view time, while a calculated column is computed once per row when data loads -- the same formula can behave very differently depending on which one it's written as.

toc_location.tile_title: DAX, Calculated Fields, and the Semantic Layer
toc_location.tile_summary: Write DAX measures in Power BI and calculated fields in Tableau, then build a centralized semantic layer that shares metric definitions across reports.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Tableau's Level of Detail expression syntax, mentioned by name as an advanced calculated-field feature outside this concept's core scope.

concepts.primary_objective: Write Tableau calculated fields to compute derived business metrics within a workbook.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a metric requirement, can the learner write a correct Tableau calculated field expression?
concepts.practice_objective: Write a Tableau calculated field computing a given business metric.
concepts.central_mental_model: A Tableau calculated field derives new data from existing fields using Tableau's own formula language, evaluated at whatever level of detail the current view aggregates to -- the same field can show different values in different visualizations.

toc_location.tile_title: DAX, Calculated Fields, and the Semantic Layer
toc_location.tile_summary: Write DAX measures in Power BI and calculated fields in Tableau, then build a centralized semantic layer that shares metric definitions across reports.

concepts.primary_objective: Build a centralized semantic layer (shared measure/field definitions) so multiple reports reuse one consistent business logic.
concepts.assessment_target: Given duplicated calculation logic across reports, can the learner centralize it into one reusable semantic definition?
concepts.practice_objective: Consolidate a calculation duplicated across 2 reports into one centralized semantic-layer definition.
concepts.central_mental_model: A semantic layer defines a business calculation once so every report that uses it agrees by construction.
